stem: A 58-year-old man with chronic exertional angina is evaluated for coronary revascularization.  Medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypercholesterolemia.  Blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg and pulse is 72/min and regular.  Cardiopulmonary examination is significant for an S4 but is otherwise normal.  Echocardiogram reveals hypokinesia of the anterior wall of the left ventricle and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%.  The patient undergoes coronary artery bypass grafting without perioperative complications.  Echocardiography is repeated 10 days after the procedure and shows that hypokinesia is no longer evident and LVEF has increased to 50%.  Which of the following myocardial processes best explains the postoperative changes in this patient's ventricular wall motion and contractility?​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​
explanation:
Myocardial hibernation is a state of reduced cellular metabolism and function that occurs in response to a sustained reduction in blood flow (and oxygen delivery) caused by coronary artery disease.

This reduced metabolic equilibrium is a protective mechanism to prevent myocardial necrosis in the setting of chronic myocardial ischemia.  Hibernating myocardium demonstrates decreased expression of contractile and cytoskeletal proteins, altered adrenergic control, and reduced calcium responsiveness.  These changes manifest as decreased contractility and impaired left ventricular (LV) systolic function.

Coronary revascularization (ie, stent placement or bypass surgery) with restoration of blood flow to hibernating myocardium restores the normal metabolic equilibrium and improves contractility and LV function.

(Choice A)  Ischemia-reperfusion injury refers to further myocardial damage that can occur due to restoration of blood flow following an episode of acute ischemia.  It is caused by increased inflammation and oxidative stress triggered by re-exposure of damaged myocardium to oxygen- and cell-rich blood.  Ischemia-reperfusion injury would reduce (not improve) contractility and LV function following revascularization.

(Choice B)  Ischemic preconditioning occurs when brief, transient episodes of myocardial ischemia activate protective signaling pathways that make the myocardium more resistant to a subsequent prolonged ischemic insult.  It is an acute protective effect, which does not explain this patients LVEF improvement after revascularization.

(Choice D)  Myocardial scarring is the replacement of myocardium with collagen and fibrous tissue, often in response to infarction and cellular necrosis.  Scarring leads to irreversible loss of myocardial contractile function such that cardiac contractility does not improve following revascularization.

(Choice E)  Ventricular remodeling refers to gradual changes in the structure or function of the heart in response to cardiac injury or hemodynamic changes (ie, pressure or volume overload).  Ventricular remodeling occurs over months to years and would not explain this patient's improved myocardial function just 10 days after revascularization.

Educational objective:Myocardial hibernation is a state of reduced metabolic function in response to chronic myocardial ischemia; it typically manifests as a reduction in myocardial contractility and ventricular systolic function.  Restoration of blood flow to hibernating myocardium restores cellular metabolism and improves contractility and ventricular function.​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​
